traditions.p: 1624 (Cutlers' Company) – present; Old Sheffield Plate 1740s–1840s; EPNS after 1840
traditions.d: The English cutlery city: fused silver-on-copper 'Old Sheffield Plate', then electroplated nickel silver, alongside steel knives and canteens.
traditions.tech: fused plate rolled from silver-clad copper ingots; later electroplating over nickel silver; forged and ground knife blades
traditions.mat: sterling silver, copper, nickel silver, stainless steel
traditions.auth: Old Sheffield Plate shows copper 'bleeding' at worn edges and has no hallmark; EPNS is stamped; 'Sheffield' marks are controlled by the Cutlers' Company.

traditions.d: Germany's 'City of Blades', home to firms making knives, scissors, razors and table cutlery.
traditions.auth: Solingen-marked steel from the city's firms; look for the maker's stamp alongside 'Solingen'.

traditions.d: France's knife capital on the Durolle river, source of most French cutting tools including laguiole-type and steak knives.
traditions.tech: forged blades; hand assembly and fitting of handles; polishing
traditions.mat: stainless and carbon steel, horn, wood, resin
traditions.auth: Le Thiers model (1993) is a registered town pattern; 'laguiole' alone is not a protected name, so check for a maker's stamp.

traditions.d: Electrolytic silver plating brought to France when Charles Christofle bought the Ruolz and Elkington patents in 1842.
traditions.tech: electroplating of silver onto nickel-silver or copper blanks
traditions.auth: Christofle pieces carry the house hallmark and plating-grade numerals; the company publishes a hallmark guide.

traditions.d: Nuribashi from Obama on Wakasa Bay: wood built up in natural lacquer with shell, pine needle and eggshell inlay, then polished to reveal the pattern.
traditions.tech: multiple lacquer layers over inlay, ground back and polished
ctr: Obama workshops (about ten master craftsmen remain)
traditions.auth: Genuine Wakasa pairs show inlay revealed through ground lacquer rather than printed patterns.

traditions.d: Tokyo hand-planed hardwood chopsticks in square to octagonal sections, sized to the user's grip.
traditions.tech: hand planing of hardwood; rounded tips
traditions.mat: ebony, red sandalwood, ironwood, Japanese box, maple
traditions.auth: Unlacquered precious hardwood with visible hand-planed facets; the name was coined by Daikokuya in 1999.

notes: Shelf: Tableware / Cutlery (B5). Old kinds k77 Table fork, k78 Table knife, k79 Table spoon, k81 Butter knife merged into one 'Cutlery set' kind with pieces as types; the 21 Gense and 5 Robert Welch range entries repeated per piece were collapsed, with Focus de Luxe, Thebe, Alveston/RW2, Radford and Bud promoted to archetypes and a short residual 'r' list (Gense Attaché/Nobel/Fuga, Robert Welch Malvern/Stanton/Caesna, Sambonet collections, Sabre Bistrot). k80 Steak knife kept with Laguiole, Perceval 9.47 and Opinel archetypes. New kinds added: Serving cutlery, Chopsticks (Wakasa, Edo kibashi archetypes), Children's cutlery (tag baby). Left out: Georg Jensen Pyramid stainless edition, Robert Welch Bud steak knife set, Radford Vintage, Christofle Albi acier and Georg Jensen Acorn chopsticks/salad servers — seen only in search snippets, pages not retrieved; Oneida/Sambonet/WMF/Puiforcat pattern years not confirmed, so Cannes, Albi, Goa and Bud carry 'undated'. Alessi Mami and WMF Stockholm are attested only via the Wikipedia Cutlery article caption. Wiki tool was unavailable (lock-file error); all sources were retrieved via web_fetch on 2026-10-12.
